clue.text: New planner on hand initially to design wind instrument for the Swiss

indicators.note: something new is made afresh, so the letters are put into a fresh order
to design is to work out a new layout, backing up the call to rearrange

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: initially asks for only the opening letter of each of the two words before it

parts.note: first letters of on and hand

explanation.surface: A new planner is told to start by designing a musical instrument for Switzerland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initially' covers both 'on' and 'hand', supplying two letters that join the planner in the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: The long wooden horn blown by herdsmen in the Alps is the classic Swiss wind instrument.

clue.text: Fantastic old actor in pageant I created

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the run of clue words that follows it

parts.note: found across the end of pageant, the I, and the start of created

explanation.surface: A grotesque performer of old appears in a show I put together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fantastic' looks like praise, but it belongs to the definition: an archaic noun for a grotesque clown or player.
explanation.definitionFit: In Elizabethan English an antic was a buffoon who performed grotesque, fantastic parts on stage, now an obsolete sense.

clue.text: One argues for replacing pen pronto

indicators.note: replacing puts things back in different positions, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone urges that a pen be replaced right away.
explanation.definitionFit: A proponent is an advocate, a person who speaks in favour of a cause or proposal.

clue.text: Does cannon explode in a flash?

indicators.note: an explosion blows things apart so the letters land in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Asks whether a cannon goes off in a flash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a flash' reads as describing the explosion; 'a flash' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A nanosecond is a billionth of a second, so it stands for an extremely brief instant.

clue.text: Clear that old boy has five pledges

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
V is the Roman numeral for five
IOUs are written promises to pay

explanation.surface: It is plain that a former pupil owes money on five promissory notes.
explanation.definitionFit: Obvious means plainly apparent, easily seen or understood.

clue.text: Itinerant is funny comedian with no English

indicators.note: funny suggests something odd or peculiar, so the letters are jumbled
with no means the following item is to be taken away

parts.note: taken as written
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A travelling performer is a comic who does not speak English.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the E from the comedian first, then shuffle the remaining seven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Nomadic means wandering from place to place, the same sense as itinerant used as an adjective.

clue.text: Confront time's aspect

parts.note: to face is to confront
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Facing up to time is one side of things.
explanation.definitionFit: A facet is one side or feature of a matter, as of a cut gem's many faces.

clue.text: Just beautiful

definitions.meaning: second meaning: lovely, as in the old phrase for a pretty lady

explanation.walkthrough: 'Just' looks like an adverb meaning 'only', but here it is the adjective meaning equitable.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective covers both impartial treatment and attractiveness, as in a poetic description of a lovely maiden.

clue.text: Heap of stones symbolising wind in empty cavern

indicators.note: in places one item inside the other
empty means the inside is cleared out, keeping just the outer letters

parts.note: first and last letters of cavern
wind is moving air

explanation.surface: A pile of rocks stands as a symbol of the wind inside a hollow cave.
explanation.definitionFit: A cairn is a mound of rough stones built as a landmark or memorial.

clue.text: Period taken to change limescale's initial impression

indicators.note: to change asks for one letter to be swapped for a different one

parts.note: the word without its opening letter, which is the one to be swapped
loosely clued: the new letter making a different impression at the start

explanation.surface: Describes how long it takes for limescale's first appearance to change.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the L at the front of limescale for T; the clue does not pin the new letter down firmly, so the definition and crossings must confirm it.
explanation.definitionFit: A timescale is the span of time allotted or needed for something to happen.

clue.text: Needle pointing north is faulty

indicators.note: something faulty is not right, so the letters must be put in a proper order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A compass needle that points north is broken.
explanation.walkthrough: The compass needle is a decoy; the needle wanted is a sharp prickle.
explanation.definitionFit: A thorn is a sharp spine on a plant, a natural needle-like point.

clue.text: Bloody exploitation of seductive woman with flag on motorway

parts.note: a vamp is a woman who seduces men
a flag is a type of iris plant
M is the abbreviation for motorway, as in the M1

explanation.surface: Reads like a lurid headline about a temptress waving a banner on a motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flag' looks like a banner, but it is the garden plant, a kind of iris.
explanation.definitionFit: Vampirism is literally feeding on blood, and figuratively preying on others, hence bloody exploitation.

clue.text: Quick and cryptic angry exchanges

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the two styles of puzzle in a newspaper
second meaning: bad-tempered words traded in a row

explanation.walkthrough: 'Quick and cryptic' looks like a description of a person's remarks, but they are two kinds of puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: Newspapers print quick and cryptic puzzles of this kind, and the phrase split in two means heated, irritated remarks.

clue.text: News heard in America of these beasts

indicators.note: heard means listened to rather than read, and in America sets the accent

parts.note: news in an American accent, with no y-sound

explanation.surface: Reports from the United States about some animals.
explanation.walkthrough: Americans say news as 'nooz', which matches the plural of the antelope, whose g is silent.
explanation.definitionFit: Gnus, or wildebeest, are large African antelopes, so they are beasts.

clue.text: Superficial likeness to musical development with added spirit

indicators.note: with added says one more item is joined on
a development changes the form of something, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
rum is a spirit drink

explanation.surface: A show's development gains a passing resemblance once some spirit is added.
explanation.walkthrough: The rum goes into the shuffle alongside the musical letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A simulacrum is an image or imitation that only resembles the real thing on the surface.

clue.text: Forces son to shift paintings

indicators.note: to shift is to move about, so the letters change places

parts.note: taken as written
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: Someone makes their son move some pictures.
explanation.definitionFit: Frescos are murals painted onto wet plaster, a kind of painting.

clue.text: Eventer prepared to fly around in a passionate way

indicators.note: around places one word on either side of the other

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: prepared means made ready, worked into a new shape

parts.note: the rider's title rearranged, though it has one E too many

explanation.surface: A horse rider gets ready to fly over a fence with great passion.
explanation.walkthrough: Fly goes around the rearranged eventer, but eventer has three Es and the answer needs only two inside FLY, so the setter has slipped. An eventer competes in horse trials.
explanation.definitionFit: Fervently means with intense, ardent feeling, which is a passionate manner.

clue.text: Wild fantasy makes me a rich eccentric

indicators.note: eccentric means off-centre and odd, so the letters are put out of order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone dreams that a mad scheme will make them a wealthy oddball.
explanation.definitionFit: A chimera is an impossible illusion or fanciful idea, named after the mythical hybrid monster.

clue.text: Reaction I've found to be successful

parts.note: an effect is a result or reaction
taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: Someone reports a response they have discovered works well.
explanation.definitionFit: Effective means producing the intended result, so it means achieving success.

clue.text: Retains particular parts of the eyeball

indicators.note: particular can mean fussy, as if someone is fiddling with the arrangement until it suits

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Seems to say an eye keeps certain of its parts.
explanation.definitionFit: The retina is the light-sensitive layer lining the back of the eye, so retinas are parts of eyeballs.

clue.text: Awful, noisy CD of a convocation

indicators.note: something awful is a mess, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A dreadful, loud recording made of some gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: A synod is a church assembly or council, so synodic means relating to such a gathering.

clue.text: Chocolate-covered fungus?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a soft sweet usually coated in chocolate or cocoa
second meaning: a prized underground mushroom

explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a mushroom dipped in chocolate; the word names both a confection and the fungus it was named after.
explanation.definitionFit: The chocolate sweet takes its name from the edible subterranean fungus, which it resembles in shape.

clue.text: The initial price demanded to get back a crossbeam

indicators.note: initial asks for the opening letter only

parts.note: first letter of The
a ransom is a sum demanded to free a captive

explanation.surface: A kidnapper's opening demand for the return of a hostage.
explanation.definitionFit: A transom is a horizontal bar across a window or above a door, so it is a cross-piece.

clue.text: Lord Lear, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps suggests a possible variant, so the letters may be put another way

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Suggests the nonsense poet Edward Lear might be a nobleman.
explanation.walkthrough: Lear looks like a name to be defined (a king, a poet), but it is just the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: An earl is a British nobleman, and nobles are addressed as Lord.

clue.text: Frilly collar said to be uneven

indicators.note: said means spoken, so the word is matched by its sound

parts.note: a ruff is a pleated Elizabethan neck frill

explanation.surface: A frilled collar is said to be lopsided.
explanation.definitionFit: Rough describes a surface that is not smooth or level, so it is bumpy.

clue.text: Not even maladjusted

explanation.walkthrough: 'Not even' reads like 'not so much as', intensifying 'maladjusted', but it is a definition in its own right.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means lopsided physically and also mentally unstable or disturbed.

clue.text: Split after daughter seen to wander

indicators.note: after says the first item named comes behind the next one

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter
a rift is a split

explanation.surface: After a family row, a daughter is seen going astray.
explanation.definitionFit: To drift is to move aimlessly, carried along without direction.

clue.text: Some retain formidable data

indicators.note: some means only part of the words that follow is taken

parts.note: found across the end of retain and the start of formidable

explanation.surface: A few people keep a huge store of information.
explanation.definitionFit: Info is the informal short form of information, which is data.

clue.text: Detour son organised to get steak

indicators.note: organised means arranged afresh, so the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A boy has arranged a diversion in order to buy some beef.
explanation.definitionFit: Tournedos is a thick round cut of beef fillet, served as steak.

clue.text: Real energy I know I initially found in alternative medicine

indicators.note: initially asks for the opening letter of each word in the list

parts.note: first letters of the five words

explanation.surface: Someone claims to have first discovered genuine energy in a complementary therapy.
explanation.definitionFit: Reiki is a Japanese healing practice channelling supposed energy through the hands, a complementary therapy.

clue.text: In Kenya, hook used to capture violent person

indicators.note: to capture is to hold inside, so the word lies within the letters

parts.note: found across the end of Kenya and the start of hook

explanation.surface: In East Africa, a hook is employed to catch a thug.
explanation.definitionFit: A yahoo is a coarse, brutish person, after the savage creatures in Gulliver's Travels.

clue.text: Cheese arrived with right decoration first

indicators.note: first says the item it follows comes ahead of the other in the order

parts.note: came is a synonym for arrived
the MBE is a British honour, Member of the Order of the British Empire
RT is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Someone turned up with the correct medal displayed foremost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First' puts the decoration before right, after the arrival.
explanation.definitionFit: Camembert is a soft, creamy French cheese from Normandy.
